description: Curated market-commentary notes on notable CDS credit-event determinations. Keyed by a lowercase entity fragment matched (word-boundary) against the determination's reference entity. Sources are freely accessible (law-firm alerts, ISDA, news); see source_url. Successor/no-event determinations are intentionally excluded.

notes.note: EMEA DC split on timing and escalated to an External Review Panel, which ruled (15 Dec 2025) a Restructuring Credit Event occurred by 29 Sep 2025 — a landmark holding that a binding TSA + consent solicitation can trigger Restructuring before the deal is implemented. ~$3.5bn gross notional across ~1,100 contracts.

First sovereign trigger of the war: EMEA DC found a Failure to Pay (2022), but OFAC sanctions blocked settlement until US Treasury General License 46 authorised a bespoke auction process (settled Sep 2022).

DC reversed itself repeatedly — no bankruptcy (5 Jun 2023) and twice no failure-to-pay (9 Jun, 7 Aug) citing waivers/conciliation — before finally declaring a Failure to Pay on 6 Sep 2023 once the 30-day grace period lapsed.

EMEA DC ruled the 15 Nov 2024 US Chapter 11 filing a Bankruptcy Credit Event; contentious because bondholders disputed whether the debt collector was genuinely distressed (no obvious liquidity crisis). Auction settled at 76 (~24% payout, ~$90m).

Bankruptcy Credit Event (accelerated safeguard, 27 May 2024). Took 22 DC meetings to settle: a 95% bond lock-up threatened to starve the auction of deliverables and skew the price — a flashpoint in the net-short / manufactured-default debate. Auction 87.75.
Bankruptcy Credit Event (30 Jul 2024) on entry into accelerated safeguard — Europe's first CDS trigger since Casino. Auction 9 Oct 2024.

Americas DC: Bankruptcy Credit Event on the Mar 2023 Chapter 11 of the Sinclair-spun regional sports networks; the group later sued parent Sinclair over ~$1.5bn of alleged misallocation. Auction 13 Apr 2023.
EMEA DC ruled Vue's debt-for-equity swap a Restructuring Credit Event (12 of 13 members in favour, 22 Mar 2023); the parallel Bankruptcy question was left open. ~$807m gross / $62m net.

Sovereign Restructuring Credit Event (19 Aug 2022) after creditors backed a two-year freeze on ~$20bn of debt amid the war; auction 28 Sep 2022. (Ukraine also had a 2015 Repudiation/Moratorium event.)
Americas DC Failure to Pay (Nov 2025) as New Fortress Energy missed term-loan interest and entered forbearance (rated SD by S&P). Recent event — limited published DC commentary so far.

Landmark first euro-area sovereign trigger: EMEA DC unanimously found a Restructuring Credit Event (9 Mar 2012) after Greece imposed retroactive collective action clauses forcing the PSI haircut on holdouts. Auction 19 Mar 2012.

Failure to Pay (30 Jul 2014) after Judge Griesa's pari passu injunction blocked payment to exchange bondholders unless holdouts were paid — a 'won't-pay vs can't-pay' selective default. Auction settled at 39.5. (Argentina also had a separate 2020 restructuring.)

The original 'manufactured' credit event: GSO (Blackstone) lent to Codere on condition it deliberately delayed a coupon past grace, engineering a Failure to Pay (18 Sep 2013) that paid out GSO's own CDS. A catalyst for later ISDA reforms.

Restructuring Credit Event (Feb 2013) after the Dutch state expropriated SNS Reaal's subordinated debt; with the sub bonds expropriated there were none to auction, so settlement ran on senior bonds — a gap that drove the new 2014 Governmental Intervention trigger.

Succession saga: after BES's 2014 resolution CDS followed bonds into Novo Banco; the Bank of Portugal's Dec-2015 retransfer of 5 bonds back to 'bad bank' BES was ruled NOT a succession event, leaving Novo Banco CDS effectively orphaned — a cautionary tale on resolution risk.

BES's Aug-2014 resolution split it into a good bank (Novo Banco) and bad bank; ISDA ruled a succession transferring CDS to Novo Banco, then the 2015 bond retransfer stranded protection buyers (see Novo Banco).

notes.entity: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena S.p.A.
notes.note: First-ever Governmental Intervention Credit Event (4 Aug 2017, on 2014-definitions subordinated trades), plus a Restructuring event on 2003-definitions trades, following Italy's 'precautionary recapitalisation' of MPS.

Bankruptcy Credit Event on the 23 Sep 2019 compulsory liquidation; notable for the CDS roll-date wrinkle (contracts expiring 20 Sep missed the trigger) and for hedge funds' CDS incentives complicating the failed rescue.

Novel intercompany / 'orphaned' event: Americas DC voted 15-0 (Dec 2016) that iHeart's election not to repay $57m of notes held by its own subsidiary was a Failure to Pay, despite arguments the payment wasn't really 'due'. ~$154m settled.

AEJ DC deadlock: the committee could not determine whether Noble's loan deferral was a Restructuring because it couldn't obtain the underlying facility documents — a 'Schrödinger's CDS' that exposed conflicts of interest among dealer members.

Bankruptcy Credit Event (10 Apr 2012) after short-seller fraud allegations and Canadian bankruptcy; the settlement was the first CDS auction ever run outside North America, Europe and Japan (Hong Kong/Singapore dealers).
Bankruptcy Credit Event (Jul 2020) after the €1.9bn accounting-fraud collapse; the DC acted on the insolvency-filing announcement, though fraud claims complicated recovery. Funds paid ~$208m.

notes.entity: Petroleos de Venezuela / Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela
notes.note: Failure to Pay for both the sovereign and PDVSA (16 Nov 2017, unanimous 15-firm DC); US sanctions (EO 13808) forced ISDA to publish a special Venezuela Protocol carving out 'restricted' debt so an auction could still function.
